questions.q: If a bar magnet is broken in two in an attempt to separate its north and south poles, what is observed?
options: An isolated north pole and an isolated south pole are finally obtained
New south and north poles appear, so each piece becomes a smaller complete magnet
The magnet loses all of its magnetism at the break
Only the north-seeking pole survives in both pieces
questions.explanation: North and south poles always occur together in equal pairs (a magnetic dipole). An isolated pole has never been observed, so breaking a magnet just produces new poles at the break, giving two smaller complete magnets.

questions.q: What is the rule describing the directions of the forces between two magnetic poles brought close together?
options: Two north poles attract; a north pole and a south pole repel
All magnetic poles attract one another regardless of type
Like poles repel; unlike poles attract
Like poles attract; unlike poles repel
questions.explanation: Two north poles repel each other and two south poles repel each other, while a north pole and a south pole attract: that is, like poles repel and unlike poles attract. The closer the poles, the stronger the force.

questions.q: How do magnetic field lines represent the direction and strength of a magnetic field?
options: Lines start at south poles and end at north poles; wider spacing means a stronger field
Lines start at north poles and end at south poles; the closer the lines, the stronger the field
Lines always cross at the poles, and crossings mark the strongest field
Line direction shows strength, while line spacing shows the field direction
questions.explanation: Magnetic field lines start at north poles and end at south poles, and their direction shows the direction of the field. The spacing of the lines shows the strength: the closer the lines, the stronger the field.

questions.q: Oersted discovered that an electric current produces a magnetic field. What shape do the magnetic field lines around a long straight current-carrying wire take, and which rule gives their direction?
options: Straight lines parallel to the wire; direction found with the left-hand rule
A bar-magnet pattern with two poles; direction found by observing the field's poles
Concentric circles around the wire; direction given by the right-hand grip rule
Radial lines pointing away from the wire; direction set by the current's speed
questions.explanation: The field lines are concentric circles. The right-hand grip rule gives the direction: the right thumb points along the conventional current that produces them.

questions.q: A long straight wire carries a current of 10 A from west to east. What is the magnetic field strength at a point 20 cm above the wire? Take the permeability of free space as \(\mu_o = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\,\mathrm{T\,m\,A^{-1}}\).
working: By the right-hand grip rule the field above the wire points from north to south.
questions.explanation: Direct substitution into \(B = \mu_o I / 2\pi r\) gives \(1 \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{T}\), directed south above the wire.

questions.q: A 2.0 A current flows through a 5 cm long thin solenoid that has 500 turns of wire. What is the magnetic field strength in the solenoid's interior? Take \(\mu_o = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\,\mathrm{T\,m\,A^{-1}}\).
working: i.e. \(25\,\mathrm{mT}\), directed along the solenoid's axis.
questions.explanation: Substituting into \(B = \mu_o N I / L\) gives \(0.025\,\mathrm{T} = 25\,\mathrm{mT}\). The field inside a solenoid is uniform, so it is independent of position.

questions.q: When a current passes through a solenoid, the magnetic field outside is similar to that of a bar magnet. How do you determine which end of the solenoid is the north pole?
options: Grip the solenoid with the right hand, fingers pointing in the direction of the conventional current; the thumb points to the north pole
Grip the solenoid with the left hand, thumb along the current; the fingers point to the north pole
The north pole is always at the end connected to the positive battery terminal
Point the right thumb along the conventional current; the thumb shows the south pole
questions.explanation: For a solenoid, grip it with the right hand so the fingers point in the direction of the conventional current around the coils; the thumb then points to the north pole. Equivalently, the end where field lines emerge is the north pole.

questions.q: Explain, in terms of magnetic domains, how a ferromagnetic material becomes magnetised.
keyPoints: A ferromagnetic material (iron, cobalt, nickel) is made up of many magnetic domains; within each domain nearly all the atomic magnets are lined up in the same direction.
When unmagnetised, the domains point in random directions so there is no overall magnetism.
When placed in a magnetic field, the domains line up in the direction of the field; when all are aligned the material is fully magnetised, or saturated.
questions.explanation: If you named domains as regions of aligned atomic magnets and described the random-to-aligned change in an external field, grade yourself Good or Easy. Missing the word 'domains' is the classic mark-loss.

questions.q: Distinguish, in terms of how easily they magnetise and retain magnetism, between soft iron and hard iron, and state which is used as the core of an electromagnet.
keyPoints: Soft iron magnetises very quickly when placed in a magnetic field and loses its magnetism very quickly when the field is removed.
Hard iron magnetises slowly but retains its magnetism for a long time, so it is used to make permanent magnets.
A solenoid with a soft iron core is an electromagnet; soft iron is used so the magnet can switch on and off cleanly with the current.
questions.explanation: Soft iron magnetises and demagnetises almost instantly, so it is used for the core of an electromagnet; hard iron retains its magnetism and is used for permanent magnets.

questions.q: The Earth behaves like a giant bar magnet. Why is the Earth's geographic North Pole actually near a magnetic south pole?
options: Because the north end of a compass needle is attracted there, and unlike poles attract
Because the geographic and magnetic poles are unrelated and just happen to coincide
Because like poles attract, so the north end of a compass is drawn to a magnetic north
Because the Earth's field reverses every day, swapping the poles
questions.explanation: A compass needle's north-seeking pole points towards geographic north. Since unlike poles attract, the pole it is attracted to must be a magnetic south. This is why the geographic North Pole sits near a magnetic south pole.
